newsitem.title: USA: Raytheon seen selling rest of appliances.
newsitem.headline: Raytheon seen selling rest of appliances.

text.p: Raytheon Co has fetched a higher price than expected from the sale of part of its appliance business and will likely sell off the remaining half of the business at a later date, analysts said.
Raytheon said Monday that it has signed a deal to sell three segments of the appliance group to privately-held Goodman Holding Co of Houston for $750 million.
"I think this is a nice move," said analyst Cai Von Rumohr of Cowen & Co. "They're getting out of a business they should have gotten out of anyway."

"There has been interest expressed in the commercial laundry business, but it would be inappropriate for us today to talk about the bids. Our options include keeping them, selling them separately, and selling them together."
Von Rumohr said analysts expected Raytheon to sell its appliance division for as much as $1 billion.
But the two remaining business could be sold for more than $300 million, which combined with the $750 realized from the three segments sold to Goodman, would raise more than $1 billion, he said.
Roger Threlfall, an analyst with J.P. Morgan, agreed.

"They kept a piece that's generating over half their operating profits and selling the rest for a high amount," he said. "Once they sell commercial laundry, they're going to get total proceeds of over $1 billion," he said.

McWade said the sale of the three segments, which includes the Amana and Caloric brands of refrigerators, freezers, microwaves, ovens and dryers, will likely have a neutral or slightly positive impact on earnings.
"When you factor in the retained earnings, we expect it to be neutral if not slightly accretive," he said.

Raytheon will keep the two commercial segments of its appliance group -- the commercial laundry and electronic control businesses -- which accounted for slightly more than 50 percent of the operating profits of the group in fiscal 1996.
The strategic assessment of the appliance group that Raytheon announced in February will continue and the two remaining units could be sold, Raytheon spokesman Bob McWade said.
"We'll continue the assessement and a sale could occur," he said.

The segments to be sold to Goodman had operating earnings of $37 million on revenues of $1.2 billion in fiscal 1996, McWade said. Conversely, the two segments Raytheon will keep had operating earnings of $38 million on revenues of $315 million, he said. The $750 sale includes $550 million in cash and $200 million in receivables, which McWade said have already been collected.

Proceeds from the sale will help pay down Raytheon's debt load, which would total about $11 billion following the proposed takeover of the Hughes Electronics Corp defense business later this year, McWade said.
